title.suggested: Tom Allen Returns to St. Louis After Six Years' Absence

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen returned to St. Louis after six years away, looking healthy, blamed 'The Parson' of Chicago for stories of his dissipation, and planned to settle and reopen his old business.

metadata.notes: Masthead: 'St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Saturday Morning, December 30, 1882', page 5.

facts.fact: Allen returned to St. Louis after about six years' absence and was welcomed at Looney's, Kelly's and other sporting resorts
Allen's old establishment, the Champion's Rest on Washington Avenue between Fourth and Fifth Streets, had been replaced by a large business building
places: Washington Avenue between Fourth and Fifth Streets, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen had sailed for England about six years earlier
His benefit in Birmingham on first returning to England was said to be the largest there since Bob Brettle's seventeen years earlier

Allen blamed a Chicago sporting man known as 'The Parson' for stories of his dissipation and drunken street brawls, saying they began because he refused to take part in hippodromes under his management
Allen said his set-to with George Rooke was agreed to involve no rough work, and that he fell only because his foot broke through the staging
Allen suffered severe sea-sickness crossing the ocean, which he blamed for his reported poor condition
Allen decided to make St. Louis his permanent home and planned to choose a location and resume his old saloon business

notes: Date and place of the Rooke set-to not stated in the article. Allen's statements are paraphrased, not direct quotes. The 1877 departure date is inferred from 'six years'.
